name: The Dealer
body:
The dealer is a specialized scoundrel that uses skills, tricks and amazing feats to confound their foes with sharpened playing cards. Power/tier wise this should be similar to the parent classes.

Hybrid Class: The martial master is a hybrid of the gunslinger and swashbuckler classes.

Role: A dealer is a ranged combatant that focuses on debilitation and control using their choice of ranged weapon.

Alignment: Any. Dealers can be of any alignment.

Some dealers adhere to the rules and use their skills to enforce them, while others use legerdemain and trickery to cheat and trick.

Hit Die: d10

Starting Wealth: 2d6 x 10 (70 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less and a deck of combat cards.

Class Skills

The dealer’s class skills are: Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Escape Artist (Dex), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), and Stealth (Dex).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier

Table: The Dealer

Class Features

The following are the class features of the dealer.

Weapon Expertise

A dealer is proficient with all simple weapons, combat cards and light armor (but no shields).

Card Combat

A dealer treats combat cards as ammunition instead of a thrown weapon as long as the deck is held in one hand and the cards are thrown with the other. The combat cards are treated as a shuriken and are recoverable. Additionally, the dealer treats their dealer levels as fighter levels for prerequisite purposes. However, feats gained in such a way are only applicable when holding or using combat cards.

Card Sharpening

A dealer can create a deck of combat cards using an existing deck of cards and an hour of work. This does not require the typical Craft check. At 3rd level the dealer can make a masterwork set of combat cards or improve an existing set to masterwork. Cards in this way are only usable as combat cards by the dealer who made them, any other character, even another dealer who attempts to use the set of combat cards made this way suffer the usual -4 improvised weapon penalty. These cards are not valuable to anyone but the dealer and are not sellable except as a set of basic playing cards, around 5 sp.

Gambit

A dealer, even a lawful one is a gambler. They fight with luck and force of personality. At the start of each day, a dealer gains a number of Gambit points equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Their Gambit goes up or down throughout the day, but usually cannot go higher than their Charisma modifier (minimum 1), though feats and magic items can affect this maximum. A dealer spends Gambit to accomplish tricks, and regains Gambit in the following ways:

Critical Hit with Combat Cards: Each time the dealer confirms a critical hit with a combat card, they regain 1 Gambit point. Confirming a critical hit on a helpless or unaware target or a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the dealer’s character level doesn’t restore Gambit.

Drawing an Ace: When using combat cards, each time a dealer pulls an ace from a standard set of 52 combat cards in combat, they regain 1 Gambit point. A dealer cannot regain more than 1 Gambit point per minute in this way.

Tricks

A dealer spends Gambit points to do tricks.

A dealer can only perform tricks of their level or lower. Unless otherwise noted, a trick can be performed multiple successive times, as long as the dealer has or spends the required number of Gambit points to perform the trick.

Bad Beat (Ex)

At 1st level, If an enemy attacks any target with a ranged or melee attack within 30 feet of the dealer, the dealer may expend a point of Gambit and an attack of opportunity to throw a combat card to attempt to deflect the attack. The dealer makes an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity; for each size category the attacking creature is larger than the dealer, the dealer takes a -2 penalty on this roll. If their attack roll result is greater than the attacker’s result, the attacking creature’s attempt automatically misses. The dealer must declare the use of this trick after the creature’s attack is announced, but before the attack roll is made.

Good Hand (Ex)

At 1st level, the dealer is an expert in using combat cards in combat. As long as the dealer has at least 1 point of Gambit remaining, the damage they deal while using combat cards is increased to 1d6. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, the damage is increased by one step, 1d8 at 5th, 1d10 at 10th, 2d6 at 15th to a maximum of 2d8 at 20th.

Poker Face (Ex)

At 1st level, a dealer can spend 1 Gambit point when they make a Bluff, Knowledge, Sense Motive or Sleight of Hand check to roll 1d6 and add the result to the check. They can do this after they make the check but before the result is revealed. If the result of the d6 roll is a natural 6, they roll another 1d6 and add it to the check. They can continue to do this as long as they roll natural 6s, up to a number of times equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

Fan of Cards (Ex)

At 3rd level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, a dealer may attack with combat cards as a melee attack so long as the dealer has at least 5 cards remaining in their deck. These attacks deal slashing damage instead of piercing damage. This allows the dealer to make melee attacks of opportunity with the cards as long as the requirements above are met at the time.

Killer Hand (Ex)

At 3rd level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, a dealer gains the ability to strike precisely with combat cards, adding their dealer level to the damage dealt. To use this trick, a dealer cannot attack with a weapon in their other hand or use a shield other than a buckler. This trick is only effective against targets within 30 ft of them. This damage is considered precision damage and any creature immune to such damage is immune to this extra damage. It also is not multiplied on a critical hit. As a swift action, a dealer can spend 1 Gambit point to double their killer hand damage bonus on the next attack. This benefit must be used before the end of their turn. Or it is lost. This trick’s cost cannot be reduced by any ability or effect that reduces the amount of Gambit points a trick costs.

Speed Deal (Ex)

At 3rd level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks. In addition, if they have the Quick Draw feat, their hands are free and unrestrained, they can draw a deck of combat cards as part of the initiative check. At 5th level, if the dealer already has a deck of combat cards drawn or they are drawn during initiative due to having the Quick Draw feat, they may always act during the surprise round.

Gambit, Luck and Panache

A Gambit pool does not stack with a luck or panache pool, but the dealer may combine pools with other classes as normal. Any feat or ability that grants more luck points or panache points adds Gambit points to your poo.

Under the Table (Ex)

At 3rd level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they can stand from prone or drop to prone as a move action without provoking an attack of opportunity. They can do this trick as a swift action by spending 1 Gambit point.

Dealers Grace (Ex)

At 7th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they take no penalty for moving at full speed when they use Acrobatics to attempt to move through a threatened area or an enemy’s space.

Card Trick (Ex)

At 7th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, the dealer can attempt a feint combat maneuver as a move action when using combat cards. At 11th level, the dealer may use this trick as a swift action.

Quick Deal (Ex)

At 7th level, the dealer may expend 1 Gambit point to make a special attack. The dealer must throw at least 10 cards and attack all creatures in a 15-foot cone. Each target must make a Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 the dealer’s class level + the dealer’s Dexterity modifier). A successful save halves this damage. If the dealer expends an entire deck of 52 cards the DC is increased by 5.

Cutting Edge (Ex)

At 11th level, when the dealer hits a living creature with a combat card attack, as a free action they can spend 1 Gambit point to have the attack deal additional bleed damage. The amount of bleed damage dealt is equal to the dealer’s Dexterity modifier (minimum 1). Alternatively, the dealer can spend 2 Gambit points to deal 1 point of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution bleed damage instead (dealer’s choice). Creatures immune to precision damage are immune to this bleed damage.

Evasive (Ex)

At 11th level, while a dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they gain the benefits of the evasion, uncanny dodge, and improved uncanny dodge rogue class features. They use their dealer levels as their rogue level for improved uncanny dodge.

Dirty Flip (Ex)

At 11th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they can make a dirty trick combat maneuver during a combat card attack. This dirty trick combat maneuver is in addition to the damage normally dealt by the combat card attack. The attack with the combat card must hit first before the combat maneuver may be attempted.

Across the Table (Ex)

At 15th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, their range with combat cards is doubled. This extra range stacks with other abilities that increase the range of the attack.

Master Gambler (Ex)

At 15th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they can take 10 on any Bluff, Knowledge, Sense Motive or Sleight of Hand check, even while distracted or in immediate danger. They can use this trick in conjunction with the poker face ability.

Perfect Flip (Ex)

At 15th level, while the dealer has at least 1 Gambit point, they can as a full round action make a single perfect throw with a combat card. When they do, they make the attack against the target’s touch AC, and ignores all damage reduction.

Cheat Death (Ex)

At 19th level, whenever the dealer is reduced to 0 hit points or fewer, they can spend all of their remaining Gambit to instead be reduced to 1 hit point. They must have at least 1 Gambit point to spend. Effects that kill the dealer outright without dealing hit point damage are not affected by this trick.

Dazing Display (Ex)

At 19th level, when using the quick deal trick, the targets that fail their Reflex saves must make a Fortitude save (at the same DC) or be dazed for 1 round.

Final Card (Ex)

At 19th level, when the dealer confirms a critical hit with a combat card or if the card is the final card in the deck of combat cards, in addition to normal damage, they can spend 1 Gambit point to make the card their final card. The target must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw or die. The DC of this save is 10 + 1/2 the dealer’s class level + the dealer’s Dexterity modifier. This is a death attack. Performing this trick does not grant the dealer a Gambit point.

Flourish (Ex)

When using the fan of cards trick, the dealer is treated as having the Weapon Finesse feat for melee attacks with combat cards, and they can use their Charisma score in place of Intelligence as a prerequisites for combat feats. This ability counts as having the Weapon Finesse feat for purposes of meeting feat prerequisites. Additionally, while using combat cards at range, the dealer may use their Dexterity modifier instead of their Strength modifier for damage.

Charmed Life (Ex)

At 2nd level, the dealer shows a knack for getting out of trouble by the skin of their teeth. Three times per day as an immediate action before attempting a saving throw, they can add their Charisma modifier to the result of the save. They must choose to do this before the roll is made. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the number of times they can do this per day increases by one (to a maximum of 7 times per day at 18th level). The dealer may use a point of Gambit to use this ability if they no longer have uses per day.

Nimble (Ex)

At 3rd level, a dealer gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the dealer to lose their Dexterity bonus to AC also causes them to lose this dodge bonus. This bonus increases by 1 for every 4 levels beyond the 3rd (to a maximum of +5 at 19th level).

Bonus Feats

At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, a dealer gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats. Dealer levels are considered fighter levels for the purposes of meeting combat feat prerequisites. In addition, upon reaching 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, a dealer can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat they have already learned. In effect, the dealer loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A dealer can only change one feat at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time they gain a new bonus feat for the level.

Dealer’s Cut (Ex)

At 5th level, a dealer gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with combat cards. While wielding combat cards, they gain the benefit of the Improved Critical feat. These attack and damage bonuses increase by 1 for every 4 levels beyond 5th level (to a maximum of +4 at 17th level).

Stacking the Decks (Ex)

Starting at 10th level, a dealer may continue to use combat cards as ammunition but only requires one hand to do so. This allows the dealer to dual wield combat cards as ammunition effectively allowing you to use two weapon fighting or with combat cards or have the other hand free to wield another weapon or shield.

Master Card (Ex)

At 20th level, the dealer has developed such incredible luck and skill that they barely notice danger. The dealer gains three additional uses of charmed life and can activate the ability as a free action, even outside of their turn. Additionally, the dealer may choose one trick. The chosen trick costs 1 less Gambit point to use. If the trick is reduced to 0 Gambit points, it instead requires you to maintain at least 1 Gambit point to use. If the trick only required you to maintain 1 Gambit point to use it, it instead may be used with or without Gambit points.

Combat Cards

Cost 40 gp; Weight 1 lb.; Damage 1d3 (small), 1d4 (medium); Critical x2; Type piercing

Range Increment 20 ft. (projectile); Category ranged; Proficiency exotic; Weapon Group thrown

A deck of combat cards holds 52 playing cards of steel, bone or wood. These cards are special in that they are sharpened for dealing damage, though still good for a playing card game.

These cards cannot be used as melee weapons. Although they are thrown weapons, combat cards are crafted as a set of 52 cards instead of individual cards. The cards are recoverable as normal thrown weapons.
